Title: Governor of Sindh appreciates government-AKU collaboration
NewsSummary: "The Aga Khan University maintains and sets standards and provides a benchmark for others to follow," stated the Governor of Sindh, His Excellency, Lt. General (Retd.) Moinuddin Haider, on a visit to the Aga Khan University (AKU) on March 2, 1999.
NewsContent:
"The Aga Khan University maintains and sets standards and provides a benchmark for others to follow," stated the Governor of Sindh, His Excellency, Lt. General (Retd.) Moinuddin Haider, on a visit to the Aga Khan University (AKU) on March 2, 1999. "I am truly motivated and inspired by this University," he added. As the first private University in Pakistan, the Governor believed AKU had provided the impetus and strength for the establishment other such institutions across the country.
 
The Governor's visit specifically focused on tile academic initiatives of the University and its collaboration with the Government on a number of social development activities in tile fields of health and education.
 
The visit commenced with a tour of tile Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU- lED) in Karimabad. Established in 1993, AKU-IED aims to improve the quality of education in Pakistan through the professional development of teachers and school heads. The Institute's works with the Government on several projects at the national as well as the provincial levels to raise educational standards in the country. In particular, there has been a close collaboration between AKU-IED and the governments of Sindh and Balochistan to upgrade the status of teachers and District Education Officers (DEOs) in these provinces.
 
The Governor then proceeded to the main AKU campus on Stadium Road, arriving at the AKU Sports Centre. Currently under construction; the Centre is scheduled for completion by the end of this year and results from the generous contributions from over 6000 young donors in Pakistan and abroad. Their contribution of Rs.150 million was matched by a similar amount from His Highness tile Aga Khan.
 
In presentations by AKU leadership, an on-going outreach effort mentioned was the AKU School of Nursing's (AKUSON) Development of women health professionals' programme, which aims to enhance the professional skills of government nurses and Lady Health Visitors. The Governor said the public sector was Beleaguered by a number of problems especially in its health management system where there was a lack of qualified nurses and paramedical personnel. He added that tile present and future collaborations between AKUSON and the Government to improve nursing practices and education in Pakistan"would add significant value to the nation's resource base,"
 
Also discussed was the University's interaction with the Government for sustainable community development through AKU's Community Health Sciences (CHS) department which provides advisory and human resource training to the Sindh Govermnent in the implementation of major health projects such as the Family Health Programme, the Thatta Health System Research Project as well as the School Nutrition Project in rural Sindh. The Governor lauded the 'on-the-ground' work of the CHS department, especially in the katchi abadis and its integral role in the addressing the country's health problems.
 
Continuing dialogue on the future initiatives of the University, the Governor commended AKU's plans to set up a College of Arts and Sciences which would offer students opportunities to study various disciplines in the humanities. Thereby broadening their minds and developing leadership qualities. The Governor agreed that the liberal education of a College of Arts and Sciences is indeed required to enable doctors, engineers and other professionals acquire an understanding of the world"beyond the rigid parameters of their disciplines." He emphasized that such an institution would be a "very valuable addition to the city of Karachi."
 
The Governor also held lively, informal and what he termed 'stimulating' dialogue with AKU medical and nursing alumni, including some who had returned to Pakistan after completing advanced formal training abroad. He praised their perseverance and commitment to their families and country and their choice to return to their home country despite better financial.
